insect noun

also bug, creepy-crawly, creepy-crawlies, bugs

classical

Cic. ND 2.123
Varr. RR 1.12.2
M-O s.v. insect

bēstiola, bēstiolae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a small creature, a bug

The everyday word for any small creature, Cicero’s and Varro’s; bēstia is the house spelling (see animal).

Other words

  • īnsectum, īnsectī n. — an insect, in the naturalists’ sense

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 11.1; Traupman 142, 333, 143; M-O s.v. insect · Declension on Wiktionary

    Pliny’s term, from insecō, to cut into; mostly plural, īnsecta.

  • cīmex, cīmicis m. — bedbug

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Andresian p. 27; Traupman 141; Traupman 284 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Andresian uses it for any bug, but classically it is the bedbug (see bedbug).

See also bedbug, ant, beetle, fly.
